plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE with confounded-batch caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, salmon-derived) and metadata.csv (12 samples: condition, batch) describe 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples where batch B1 = all controls and batch B2 = all treated — a design in which condition and batch are perfectly confounded (correlation = 1). This is not a nuisance to correct: no statistical method (ComBat-seq, SVA, removeBatchEffect, or a batch term in the model) can separate a condition effect from a batch effect here, because the model matrix would not be full rank. The only defensible path is (1) confirm the confound empirically via sample-structure QC, (2) fit condition alone with DESeq2, and (3) label every downstream result — DE genes, fold changes, and enriched pathways — as confounded, i.e. consistent with either a treatment effect, a technical/batch artifact, or both, with no way from this dataset alone to distinguish them. The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 workflow (raw-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage, BH-adjusted independent filtering) and closes with fgsea preranked enrichment against MSigDB Hallmark (available locally) and WikiPathways human as a second collection, followed by a report that states the confound explicitly per the flagged rule R-0005.
